articles.title: At just 19, Dak Prescott faced a heartbreaking loss that changed his life forever, but the pain he carried helped shape the NFL star he would eventually become
articles.summary: Dak Prescott has spent years being known as the face of the Dallas Cowboys, but his journey to becoming an NFL star was shaped by a life that tested him
articles.body: Dak Prescott has spent years being known as the face of the Dallas Cowboys, but his journey to becoming an NFL star was shaped by a life that tested him long before he reached the biggest stage in football. He was still a young college quarterback when his mother, Peggy, was diagnosed with Stage 4 colon cancer. A few years later, he lost his older brother Jace to suicide. Those losses left a permanent mark on Dak, but they also changed the way he looked at his own life. Instead of allowing grief to define him, he used it to help others and became an outspoken voice for cancer awareness and mental health.Dak Prescott lost his mother while his football dream was still taking shapePeggy Prescott was more than Dak’s mother. She was one of the people who helped shape the person he would become.In the summer of 2012, Peggy was diagnosed with Stage 4 colon cancer. She was only 52. At the time, Dak was playing college football at Mississippi State and trying to establish himself as a quarterback. His life was already moving toward football, but suddenly, his family was facing something far more important than a game.Peggy continued to support her son while going through treatment. She made an effort to attend his games whenever she could, even as cancer took a growing toll on her health. For Dak, those moments became memories he would carry for the rest of his life.Peggy died on November 3, 2013, after an approximately year-and-a-half battle with cancer. Dak was still in college and had not yet become the NFL quarterback millions of people would eventually know.Losing his mother at such an important point in his life could have completely changed his path. Instead, it became part of the motivation he carried with him.Dak has repeatedly spoken about the influence his mother had on him. He has called her his moral compass and has continued to honor her through his football career and charitable work. When he received the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award following the 2022 season, he dedicated the honor to Peggy.But the loss did not end with his mother’s death.Years later, another devastating tragedy hit the Prescott family.In April 2020, Dak’s older brother, Jace Prescott, died at 31. Dak later revealed that Jace had died by suicide. The loss was especially painful because Jace had carried a heavy responsibility within the family during Peggy’s illness and had served as one of her primary caregivers.Dak was now dealing with another loss involving someone he loved deeply.The timing made everything even harder. Jace’s death came during the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic, when much of the world was experiencing isolation and uncertainty. Dak was also dealing with the aftermath of a serious ankle injury that threatened to interrupt his football career.For someone who had already experienced the death of his mother, the loss of his brother brought another wave of grief.Dak eventually began speaking openly about what he was going through. He talked about anxiety, depression and the importance of getting professional help instead of trying to carry everything alone.That was an important part of his story because Dak was not simply dealing with personal grief. He was also one of the NFL’s biggest stars, playing a position where athletes are often expected to appear strong no matter what is happening behind the scenes. He chose to talk about it anyway.From a grieving son and brother to one of the NFL’s most recognizable namesDak’s football career continued to rise even while his personal life was filled with challenges.The Dallas Cowboys selected him in the fourth round of the 2016 NFL Draft, with the 135th overall pick. He quickly became the team’s starting quarterback and developed into one of the most recognizable players in the league.But the success did not erase what had happened before it.If anything, Dak found a way to carry his family with him.In 2017, he launched the Faith. Fight. Finish. Foundation, inspired by his mother’s battle with cancer. The name came from the words and attitude Peggy carried during her fight.The foundation initially focused heavily on cancer awareness, research and helping families affected by the disease. After Jace’s death, its work expanded to include mental health and suicide prevention.That connection between his two biggest losses became central to Dak’s work away from football.He has spoken about wanting Jace’s death to have a purpose by helping other people seek support before reaching a crisis. Rather than keeping his grief private, he used his position as a high-profile athlete to start conversations that many people still find difficult to have.That has become one of the most meaningful parts of Dak’s story.He could have allowed people to see only the quarterback wearing the Cowboys star, throwing touchdowns in front of millions of fans. Instead, he has also allowed them to see the son who lost his mother, the brother who lost Jace and the person who struggled with his own mental health.His journey shows that success does not mean a person stops carrying their difficult memories. Sometimes, it means learning how to carry them differently.Dak has continued to honor Peggy by supporting cancer awareness and encouraging people to take colon cancer seriously. He has honored Jace by speaking about mental health and suicide prevention and by supporting efforts designed to help people who may be struggling.His story is therefore bigger than his statistics or the Cowboys jersey he wears.The boy who watched his mother battle a devastating illness eventually became an NFL quarterback. The son who lost his mother while still in college went on to become a national sports figure. The younger brother who lost Jace later used his platform to encourage people to ask for help when they are struggling.That does not make the losses any less painful, and Dak has never suggested that they are. Instead, he has found a way to let those losses influence the person he wants to be.Football gave Dak Prescott a platform, but his experiences gave that platform a deeper purpose. His mother and brother remain part of his story, not simply as painful memories, but as the reason he continues to use his success to help other people.For Dak, becoming a famous NFL quarterback was only one part of the journey. The more powerful part has been what he chose to do after life gave him reasons to stop.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kelly Stafford can’t resist thirsting over Erin Andrews from 40,000 feet while watching her on TV
articles.summary: Kelly Stafford was 40,000 feet in the air, watching NFL on Fox off a seatback screen, when she decided the game itself wasn't the main event.
articles.body: Kelly Stafford was 40,000 feet in the air, watching NFL on Fox off a seatback screen, when she decided the game itself wasn't the main event. Erin Andrews was. The reigning MVP's wife caught Andrews doing her sideline reporter thing, mic in hand, blonde hair blowing, full pro mode, and couldn't resist complimenting her.Kelly Stafford Gushes Over Erin Andrews Mid-Flight: "Girl Looking Good at 40,000 Feet""Girl looking good at 40,000 feet 🔥," Stafford wrote on her Instagram story, tagging @erinandrews. One flame emoji, doing the work of a whole paragraph. Here's the thing about Kelly Stafford, she didn't need to say anything. She's mid-flight, minding her business, catching a game like the rest of us. And she still paused to hand out a compliment to another woman on live television. That's not just a nice thing to say, that's a whole energy. Kelly Stafford is out here throwing flowers at cruising altitude, no occasion required.It tracks, too. This isn't new behavior from her. Stafford has made a habit of hyping up the women around the league, she's previously played "elder NFL WAG," dishing out advice to the likes of Brittany Mahomes and Taylor Swift about not losing themselves in the chaos of football-wife life. So an unprompted, flirty shoutout to a sideline reporter mid-flight? Very on-brand. She's basically been running a one-woman support system for women in football for years now, and Erin Andrews just got pulled into the group chat.Meanwhile, her own husband is having quite the year to watch from a plane seat. Matthew Stafford is coming off a genuinely wild 2025, he led the league with 4,707 passing yards and a ridiculous 46 touchdowns, walking away with the NFL MVP award at 37 years old, because apparently age is just a number when Sean McVay is calling your plays. The Rams rewarded him with a one-year, $55 million extension that locks him in through the 2027 season, so no offseason drama this time around.2026 has been more of a rollercoaster so far. Stafford opened the season quietly with just 155 yards and an interception in the Week 1 loss before roaring back in Week 2 with 327 yards and four touchdowns in a blowout win over the Giants, doing it without star receiver Puka Nacua, who sat out with a hip injury. Reigning MVP energy, on and off.So while Matthew's out there rewriting his own legacy on the field, Kelly's clearly just enjoying the ride, catching the game from a plane, snack in hand, and still finding time to compliment a colleague's on-camera glow-up. Multitasking at its finest.No word yet on whether Erin Andrews has seen the shoutout. But if she has, we'd bet on a smile and maybe a follow-back compliment.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, has made an impressive comeback after a slow run on the field in the last season.
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, has made an impressive comeback after a slow run on the field in the last season. During the 2025 NFL regular season, Travis Kelce caught 76 receptions for 851 receiving yards and scored 5 touchdowns in 17 games for the Kansas City Chiefs as many demanded he retire. Across the last two games, the Super Bowl champion has broken records and now Jason Kelce has opened up about it.Jason Kelce opens up about Travis Kelce’s achievements amid his record breaking performance in the new seasonA few days ago, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player Jason Kelce opened up about Travis Kelce while casting his “Himmy Award” selection on Monday Night Countdown, as he said, “Alright I’m going with my little brother…”Jason Kelce added, “He just broke the all-time YAC [yards after catch] receiving record,” he continued.The former Philadelphia Eagles’ star icon added, “Like it’s hard to even fathom that he just passed guys like Marshall Faulk, Terrell Owens, Steve Smith. This record is one of the all-time, most impressive things…What you do after the catch, how much you try to make something happen.”For the unversed, in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season against the Denver Broncos, Travis Kelce caught a 59-yard pass to surpass Jason Witten for second place all-time in career receiving yards by a tight end.In an interview, Travis Kelce reflected on his achievement as he said, “I had no idea, I had no idea. It was pretty freaking cool man, to be in the talks with guys like Marshall Faulk, Larry Fitz, Terrell Owens; that’s some pretty cool stuff man.”Jason Kelce has remained Travis Kelce’s strongest support system as the tight end navigates through constant spotlightIn the last few years, there has been a considerable amount of buzz around Travis Kelce’s personal life as his high profile wedding made billions curious.Amid this, Travis Kelce’s older brother Jason Kelce has been there for him through all the challenging days that he has faced.While Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce have had a pretty successful career in the league, they have also been entrepreneurial and are working on multiple businesses together.This includes their popular podcast, New Heights, which signed a $100 million deal in 2024 with Amazon’s Wondery.Apart from their podcast, Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce are also the co-owners of Garage Beer while they have invested in a lot of start ups together.Jason Kelce has also been spotted at most matches as he is spotted cheering on his brother.For now, all eyes remain on the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player and popular tight end Travis Kelce as he eyes a Super Bowl this season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ business venture gets a massive $10.1 billion valuation boost
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Patrick Mahomes’ business portfolio received a major boost when Whoop secured a fresh $575 million funding round at a $10.1 billion
articles.body: Earlier this year, Patrick Mahomes’ business portfolio received a major boost when Whoop secured a fresh $575 million funding round at a $10.1 billion valuation. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback backed the fitness technology company years before its latest rise, making his early investment a notable part of the story. Whoop’s growth also highlights how athlete-backed ventures can develop far beyond their original niche, with the company now serving millions of members worldwide and expanding its focus on performance, recovery and long-term health.Patrick Mahomes’ Whoop investment gets a major boostMahomes invested in Whoop in 2020, when the company was valued at about $1.2 billion. At the time, the wearable brand was building its reputation around sleep, recovery and strain tracking, particularly among professional athletes.That early connection has continued beyond business. Mahomes has used Whoop during his football career and has also appeared in promotional campaigns with his wife, Brittany Mahomes. He later celebrated the company's latest funding announcement on social media.The new round was led by Collaborative Fund and included major investors such as Qatar Investment Authority, Mubadala Investment Company, Abbott and Mayo Clinic. Several prominent athletes, including Cristiano Ronaldo, LeBron James and Rory McIlroy, are also associated with Whoop.Founder and CEO Will Ahmed announced the latest milestone, saying:“I am pleased to announce that we’ve raised $575M at a $10.1B valuation to accelerate our mission of unlocking human performance and healthspan globally,”The company reportedly has more than 2.5 million members and ended 2025 cash-flow positive. Its subscriptions also grew sharply during the year.Patrick Mahomes balances Whoop success with strong NFL returnMahomes’ off-field success comes as he has also made a strong return to NFL action. After recovering from the torn ACL and LCL that ended his 2025 season, the Chiefs quarterback has started all three games of the 2026 campaign.Kansas City opened the season with a 31-10 win over Denver before Mahomes delivered a 382-yard, three-touchdown performance in a 33-30 overtime victory against Indianapolis.In Week 3, Mahomes added two touchdown passes and 246 passing yards as the Chiefs beat Miami 24-10, improving to 3-0. He also connected with Travis Kelce for a 48-yard gain on Kansas City’s opening snap.The quick return has added another layer to Mahomes’ Whoop connection. The company’s technology is built around tracking strain, recovery and sleep, areas that have particular relevance for an athlete coming back from a major knee injury. articles.title: How Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld got engaged, married, and announced a baby in less time than most NFL contracts get negotiated
articles.summary: Most NFL players spend their off-seasons rehabbing knees or renegotiating contracts.
articles.body: Most NFL players spend their off-seasons rehabbing knees or renegotiating contracts. Josh Allen spent his getting married, announcing a pregnancy, and welcoming a baby girl. The Buffalo Bills quarterback and actress Hailee Steinfeld went from their first public sighting in May 2023 to a Santa Barbara wedding, a pregnancy announcement, and a newborn daughter by April 2026. That is roughly 35 months. The average NFL contract negotiation drags longer. What unfolded between them is worth paying attention to, not because it was loud, but precisely because it was not.How did Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld go from first sighting to wedding so quickly?The timeline moves fast, but the early stages did not. When Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld were first spotted together in New York in May 2023, neither confirmed anything. Allen was asked directly during an appearance on the Pardon My Take podcast. He deflected with a joke, playing on the Seinfeld spelling, and said he had a "girlfriend" without ever using her name. For over a year, they moved quietly.That changed in July 2024. Allen posted a carousel on Instagram that included a photo of the two of them on a balcony in Paris, looking out at the Eiffel Tower. No caption explaining it. No announcement. Just the image, sitting there in the middle of other vacation photos. Host Kay Adams called it his "hard launch" on Up and Adams shortly after. Allen smiled and said, "We love love." That was essentially the whole statement.Four months after going public, he proposed. November 22, 2024. The setting was oceanside, with candles and a pink floral arch. Steinfeld later said in an interview with Who What Wear that Allen made sure she was dressed up for the day and still caught her completely off guard. The engagement photos went up on Instagram without a press release or a planned media rollout. By NFL standards, that kind of restraint is almost unusual.On May 31, 2025, they married at San Ysidro Ranch in Santa Barbara. Steinfeld wore three custom Tamara Ralph dresses across the day. Her father walked her down the aisle. There were no papped shots on the way in, no coordinated magazine exclusive the morning after. The couple controlled what got out and released it on their own terms.Writing in her Beau Society newsletter after the wedding, Steinfeld described the experience: "Over the past two weeks, random yet very specific memories have been popping back into our heads, and we've been blurting them out to each other, often through smiles, laughs, and tears. It felt like love was running through the veins of every tree at our gorgeous venue in Santa Barbara." That is not a PR quote. That reads like someone who meant it.What has Hailee Steinfeld said about life with Josh Allen after welcoming their baby girl?December 12, 2025. Allen posted a video on Instagram showing him kissing Steinfeld's pregnant belly. That was the pregnancy announcement. Simple, direct, no countdown clock or gender reveal party broadcast. Steinfeld was already visibly pregnant when she attended the 83rd Golden Globe Awards on January 11, 2026, without Allen, who was busy leading the Bills to a win over the Jacksonville Jaguars that same day. She wore a blush pink gown embellished with silver beads and stood on the red carpet for a film, Sinners, that was nominated for best motion picture drama.In April 2026, Steinfeld sent her Beau Society newsletter subscribers a quiet update. The baby had arrived. A girl. She did not post on Instagram first or schedule a morning show appearance. She told the people who had been reading her newsletter that the baby was here and she was happy. "To say we are unbelievably happy and in love with this baby girl would be an understatement," she wrote. "I'm soaking in the newborn bliss."What stands out across the entire arc of this relationship is how consistently they have avoided performing it. Allen went from playing coy on a podcast to being a married father in just over two years. Steinfeld went from award-season press runs to writing about newborn mornings in a newsletter she controls. Neither of them handed this story to a tabloid. They just lived it, and let the moments speak when they felt ready.In a media landscape where NFL relationships are often turned into content pipelines the moment they become public, that approach is harder to pull off than it looks.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "He looked like a cancer patient": Tom Brady’s painful final attempt to save his marriage with Gisele Bündchen revealed
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s private struggle during the final months of his marriage to Gisele Bündchen has come under fresh scrutiny.
articles.body: Tom Brady’s private struggle during the final months of his marriage to Gisele Bündchen has come under fresh scrutiny. A new biography about the seven-time Super Bowl champion details an 11-day break he took from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022 as he tried to work through personal issues. The account also describes how deeply the situation appeared to affect Brady’s physical appearance and mood, according to people around the team at the time.Tom Brady’s marriage struggle reportedly took a physical tollThe details come from Lars Anderson’s upcoming biography, Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, which is scheduled for release on September 29. Anderson drew on more than 350 interviews for the book, although Brady himself did not participate in the project.According to an excerpt reported ahead of the book’s release, people around the Buccaneers noticed a significant change in Brady during the period when his marriage was under severe strain. The book says he lost close to 20 pounds, prompting concern among those who knew him.Former Buccaneers head coach Bruce Arians connected the weight loss to the pressure Brady was facing in his personal life.“For Tom to lose that much weight, on his frame, it was a lot. It was very clear that the reason for the weight loss was the stress from the personal issues he was dealing with,”Another coach offered an even more striking description of Brady’s appearance at the time:“With all respect, he looked like a cancer patient with really good hair. He just seemed miserable, not even close to the Tom we all loved. He was so stressed.”The comments describe how noticeable the change was to people inside the Buccaneers organisation. They do not establish a medical diagnosis, but they reflect the concern surrounding Brady’s condition during that period.Tom Brady’s 11-day attempt to save his marriage to Gisele BündchenThe biography also details Brady’s reported decision to step away from the Buccaneers during training camp in 2022. He told quarterback coach Clyde Christensen that he needed time to deal with “some personal things” before travelling to the Bahamas.According to the book, Brady met Bündchen at a private resort during the 11-day absence in an attempt to work through their marital problems. When he returned to the team, Christensen reportedly felt that Brady seemed profoundly changed, describing him as an “empty shell.”The couple ultimately announced their divorce in October 2022 after more than a decade of marriage. The new account offers another glimpse into the difficult period before their split, while much of the couple’s private relationship remains known only to Brady and Bündchen.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jameis Winston Dedicates Giants' Win vs. Titans to Jaxson Dart After QB's Season-Ending Knee Injury
articles.summary: After leading the New York Giants to a 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, veteran quarterback Jameis Winston sent an epic message to second-year signal-caller Jaxson Dart.
articles.body:
After leading the New York Giants to a 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, veteran quarterback Jameis Winston sent an epic message to second-year signal-caller Jaxson Dart.

Winston told reporters after the game that Sunday's win was dedicated to Dart, who suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2.

"There was no doubt on the sideline that it was gonna happen," Winston said. "We are our brother's keeper, winning this game for Jaxson. 12 points, six times two, it's for you."

Winston threw for only 118 yards in the win, but he received an endorsement from head coach John Harbaugh, who said after the game that he expects the 32-year-old to remain New York's starter even if the team adds another quarterback following Dart's injury.

Winston and the Giants (2-1) will try to keep the momentum going when they meet the Arizona Cardinals (1-1) in Week 4.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson goes from Cleveland villain to hero in Browns upset win, as home crowd turns jeers to cheers
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson turned Cleveland's Dawg Pound boos into "Let's go Watson" chants with a fourth-quarter comeback against the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body: There was a stunning upset in Cleveland on Sunday as the Browns beat the favored Carolina Panthers , but it had nothing to do with the outcome and everything to do with quarterback Deshaun Watson. The dude turned the hometown crowd's boos to cheers. The people who have grown to seriously dislike their starting quarterback, many of them angrily barking at him from the Dawg Pound in all sorts of unfriendly tones, were actually chanting, "Let's go Watson" before this game was over. DESHAUN WATSON THROWS INTERCEPTION FIVE SNAPS INTO 2026 SEASON AS BROWNS GET OFF TO ROUGH START About the only boos Watson could hear in the second half of this one was when he was sacked during a crucial third down by Carolina edge rusher Princely Umanmielen for a seven-yard loss, but replays on the big screens showed Umanmielen grabbing and twisting Watson’s facemask without a call from an official. There hasn't been a turnaround like this since Apple Inc. rose from near bankruptcy in the 1990s. Watson barely heard anything other than approval from the home crowd. Well, maybe a smattering of boos earlier. "I was hearing the crowd, the yelling the positivity," Watson said afterward. "That's my main focus. I didn't hear any of [the boos], but at the same time, I was just trying to give them something to cheer about and we got that W so that's all that matters." Stunning. These words seem foreign to anyone who heard that press conference Watson gave during the preseason when he called the home crowd "disrespectful" for booing him when he injured his Achilles in 2024 and then again in the preseason when he played his first game back at Huntington Bank Field. He added that it was "personal" between him and the crowd and having nothing to do with his performance. And, well, it has something to do with performance. Watson's two passing touchdowns and the comeback win proved that because suddenly the folks who didn't like him very much previously seemed to approve. DESHAUN WATSON HARBORS NO ILL WILL TOWARD CLEVELAND AFTER COLLECTING $184M FOR 19 TDS IN FOUR SEASONS But, yes, maybe some of the ire Watson felt from fans previously was because of his huge contract, and inability to live up to the money the past four years, and the NFL suspension Watson had to accept in 2022, and the reason for that suspension, which was tied to alleged sexual assaults of two dozen female massage therapists. All of that made Browns fans unwilling to cut their quarterback a break. But Watson seemed to win some of them back, at least for one afternoon, when his team erased a 12-10 deficit in the fourth quarter. No, it didn't take a lot. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! This was, by the way, Watson's first regular-season home game of this season and first since that 2024 game in which he ruptured his Achilles. So, a big deal. "From the moment I woke up, just the anticipation, just the anxiousness, just everything, just to get in front of the fans, just to get here, just to get started," Watson said in describing what drove him. "I wanted to play perfect so bad, but, you know, that's the NFL with its ups and downs ... The energy, the fans, it was amazing. They kept believing in us. They kept the energy up ... And we just continued to feed off that energy of the crowd." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: How Travis Kelce's 7 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons became the financial blueprint that unlocked every major endorsement deal he ever signed
articles.summary: Travis Kelce's $90 million net worth did not arrive because he was famous. It arrived because he was relentless.
articles.body: Travis Kelce's $90 million net worth did not arrive because he was famous. It arrived because he was relentless. Between 2016 and 2022, he recorded at least 1,000 receiving yards in seven straight seasons, a streak no tight end in NFL history has ever matched. That consistency on the field was never just a football story. It was a financial strategy, whether Kelce consciously framed it that way or not. Every brand that eventually wrote him a check was paying for that track record, not his personality.How did Travis Kelce's on-field consistency lead to major brand deals?Endorsement deals in the NFL rarely go to the most talented player in the room. They go to the most predictable one. Brands need athletes who show up, perform, and do it again the following year. Travis Kelce gave them exactly that for seven consecutive seasons.He started with Nike and State Farm. Then came McDonald's, Bud Light, Sleep Number, Tide, and eventually Pfizer. None of these brands stumbled onto Kelce by accident. They were watching someone who caught 103 passes for 1,336 yards in 2018, then came back and did 1,229 yards in 2019, then broke the single-season tight end record with 1,416 yards in 2020. Year after year, the number above 1,000 kept appearing next to his name.That kind of durability is rare at any position. At tight end, a physically punishing spot where careers often peak and collapse before 30, it was almost unheard of. Kelce turned 30 during that streak and kept going. That mattered to marketing teams more than any single highlight reel ever could.His contract history tells the same story from a different angle. He signed a five-year, $46 million extension in 2016, the same year he first crossed 1,000 yards. By 2020, a four-year, $57.25 million deal followed. In 2024, the Chiefs restructured his contract with an average annual value of $17.125 million, briefly making him the highest-paid tight end in the league. The math was straightforward: sustained production drove sustained leverage.How did Travis Kelce use football success to build a business empire off the field?The seven-year streak did something else. It bought Travis Kelce credibility in rooms that had nothing to do with football. When he and his brother Jason launched New Heights in 2022, it was not a vanity project. It was built on the accumulated trust of a decade of elite performance. People tuned in because Travis Kelce had earned the right to be heard.Amazon's Wondery saw that clearly enough to sign a three-year, $100 million distribution deal in August 2024. That figure dwarfs his $12 million Chiefs salary for the 2026 season. Think about that for a moment. The podcast now generates more guaranteed annual income than the sport that made him famous.His investments followed the same pattern of earned trust. Casa Azul Tequila, Garage Beer, Hilo Nutrition, Club Car Wash, and 1587 Prime, the Kansas City steakhouse he co-owns with Patrick Mahomes. None of these deals would have landed the same way for a tight end who had one good season. They landed because Kelce built something over time that made investors and brand partners feel safe.His fame expanded further when Taylor Swift started attending Chiefs games in 2023. The couple married in July 2026, and their combined net worth now sits at $1.89 billion. But Kelce's $90 million was already built before any of that cultural crossover arrived. He had already done the work.Fourteen seasons into his NFL career, Kelce has career earnings of approximately $123.2 million from football alone. Add the podcast, the endorsements, the equity stakes, and the media work, including a role in Ryan Murphy's Grotesquerie and hosting Are You Smarter Than a Celebrity on Prime Video, and the $90 million figure starts to look conservative.Most athletes reach the end of their playing careers and then figure out what comes next. articles.body:
Jameis Winston didn't have a banner day during his team's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday in rainy conditions, throwing for 118 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and three sacks taken while the offense managed just 238 total yards.

But the Giants don't seem to have any plans to replace him as the starter, at least for the time being.

"Yes. Yes, I do," head coach John Harbaugh told reporters Sunday when asked if he believes Winston will remain atop the depth chart. "Yes, I do."

The Giants don't seem inclined to change their quarterbacking plans just yet.

"Not at all. The plans are the plans. The opportunities that you have are the opportunities you have," Harbaugh told reporters while discussing whether Winston's play would affect the team's plans for the starting quarterback position. "No matter what, we're going to do everything we can to make our team as strong as we can based on what options we have."

Winston has replaced Jaxson Dart, who is out for the remainder of the regular season with a knee injury. That put a major dent in the team's playoff aspirations, though Sunday's win brought them to 2-1 on the season. And Winston has the trust of the locker room.

"We did win, didn't we? We trust our guy back there," center John Michael Schmitz said. "We trust that he can get the job done. We've got all the belief in him as our quarterback."

articles.title: Kirk Cousins and the Raiders improve to 3-0, their best start in years, with comeback win over Saints
articles.summary: The Raiders are still perfect on the season, and reigning No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza hasn't played a snap yet.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders are still perfect.

The Raiders rallied late, and took advantage of a few bad turnovers, to beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 at the Caesars Superdome on Sunday afternoon. That moved the Raiders to 3-0 on the year, which is their best start since the 2021 campaign. The Raiders won three straight to open that season before finishing 10-7 and earning a playoff berth.

The Saints looked like they were going to grab a pretty convincing win on Sunday, thanks to a career day from quarterback Tyler Shough . He threw four touchdowns on the day, a pair to both tight ends Noah Fant and Juwan Johnson . The last touchdown, a 16-yard toss to Fant, put them up by 11 at the time.

But then things went downhill for New Orleans . In the fourth quarter, the Raiders got to Shough and forced a fumble, which Maxx Crosby recovered to set up the go-ahead touchdown — a 4-yard pass from Kirk Cousins to Cody White .

Then, just three plays later, Shough threw a bad interception right to rookie Hezekiah Masses, who ran it back into scoring position. That led to a touchdown, too, this time a four-yard pass to Brock Bowers .

Shough got the Saints into scoring position one last time, thanks in part to a huge 22-yard pass to Johnson.

But once again, Shough fumbled it away. Jeremy Chinn drilled Shough in the backfield to force the fumble.

The Saints did get the ball back one final time, but Johnson fumbled it away, too. That turnover, the fourth in the fourth quarter alone, was enough to seal the deal for the Raiders.

Shough ended up going 29-of-42 for 255 yards with four touchdowns and an interception in the loss, which dropped the Saints to 1-2 on the year.

Cousins went 22-of-33 for 248 yards with three touchdowns in the win for Las Vegas . Ashton Jeanty had 56 yards on 19 carries, and Bowers had 116 yards and a touchdown on 10 catches.

The Raiders still have a long way to go to actually earn what would be just their second postseason berth since relocating to Nevada. The franchise hasn't won a playoff game since the 2002 campaign, either, when it fell to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the Super Bowl.

But winning three in a row to open the season is a great start for the franchise that has had six different head coaches in the past six seasons. First-year head coach Klint Kubiak is well on his way, and he's done it all without their No. 1 overall draft pick, Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, playing a single snap.

With how things are going so far this fall, it's hard to imagine Kubiak and the Raiders will be rushing to turn to their presumed quarterback of the future, either. Cousins has things handled just fine.

articles.title: Ravens Beat Cowboys, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Dak, Lamar Jackson, Henry, Lamb, Top Players
articles.summary: It took one play for the Baltimore Ravens to get kicker Tyler Loop into field goal position and seal a 34-31 victory over the Dallas Cowboys with one second remaining in regulation.
articles.body:
It took one play for the Baltimore Ravens to get kicker Tyler Loop into field goal position and seal a 34-31 victory over the Dallas Cowboys with one second remaining in regulation.

The duel at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, saw the Ravens as 3.5-point favorites over the Cowboys, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , with both teams entering the matchup at 1-1.

Just as it looked like the game was headed for overtime, tied at 31 with seven seconds remaining, Lamar Jackson connected with Zay Flowers for 27 yards to set up Loop for a 56-yard dagger and seal the win in Brazil.

Dallas found the end zone first with 4:32 remaining in the opening quarter on a Javonte Williams rushing touchdown.

Baltimore's Derrick Henry responded on the next drive with a direct snap touchdown, but Dallas entered the second quarter with a 10-7 advantage with the addition of a successful field goal.

The Ravens began their push for the lead in the second quarter behind Henry's second touchdown of the day, a defensive fourth-down stop and a field goal, to enter halftime with a 17-13 lead.

Dallas was fortunate Baltimore did not run away with the game in the third quarter, committing a fumble on its opening drive and suffering a blocked field goal attempt.

The Cowboys held the Ravens to a touchdown while notching one of their own on a Jake Ferguson reception to trail by just three heading into the final quarter.

Dallas' defense came up big with a fourth-down stop to open the fourth quarter, followed by a 96-yard drive that ended with a touchdown from KaVontae Turpin to give the Cowboys a four-point lead.

Jackson and the Ravens did what they do best, answering with a Matthew Hibner touchdown to retake the lead by three with 1:30 remaining and put the Cowboys' backs against the wall.

The Cowboys stormed down the field and nailed what seemed to be the field goal to force overtime before Baltimore's miraculous one-play drive set up the game-winning kick.

Baltimore will return home to host the Tennessee Titans next Sunday, while Dallas will stay in Texas but head to Houston to face the Texans that same day.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 3 Results, Who Could Bucs & Chargers Take?
articles.summary: Three of the five 0-3 teams in the NFL were not expected to struggle this much going into the regular season.
articles.body:
Three of the five 0-3 teams in the NFL were not expected to struggle this much going into the regular season.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in possession of the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft order after Sunday afternoon's games.

The Houston Texans, Tennessee Titans, Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins are in that order behind the Texans.

Houston, Tampa Bay and Los Angeles were projected to be closer to the tops of their respective divisions, instead of in the early discussion for the No. 1 overall pick.

Quarterbacks have been the talk of the 2027 draft class, but if these teams remain at the top of the draft order, players like Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith and Texas edge-rusher Colin Simmons could be in play for the top pick.

8. New York Jets (via Indianapolis -1-2)

15. Cleveland (via Los Angeles Rams - 1-2)

Jeremiah Smith has a strong case to make as the No. 1 overall pick one month into the college football regular season.

The Ohio State wide receiver already has 617 yards and seven touchdowns on 33 receptions through four games.

Smith set career highs across the board on Saturday with 12 receptions, 217 yards and four touchdowns.

All of the teams currently in the top five of the projected draft order could use a playmaker like Smith in their offense.

Houston has been almost too reliant on Nico Collins and needs a complement, or a new No. 1, to add to C.J. Stroud's offense.

The Chargers could use a standout No. 1 wide out to go with Justin Herbert. That would make the offense far more dangerous with Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston in supporting roles.

Tampa Bay could use Smith as well, even with Emeka Egbuka and a young core already in place.

The Titans and Dolphins need help everywhere across the field, so they would love if Smith land with them, if they aren't in the quarterback market.

It's hard to imagine that, regardless of team, Smith falls outside of the top five because he has franchise-changing talent.

Colin Simmons made his case to be the top defensive player in the 2027 NFL draft with his performance on Saturday.

The Texas edge-rusher had five sacks in the Longhorns' win over the Tennessee Volunteers.

Simmons has a sack in three of his four games so far this season. He also has a fumble recovery and a fumble forced.

Simmons would be an ideal fit for most defenses. He could be a top-five pick because of how much of an impact he can make on any team, whether it be a contender, or a rebuilding team.

Simmons will have plenty of other chances to impress since the Longhorns have multiple Top 25 matchups left on their SEC schedule.

articles.body: Life is pretty sweet if you're a Jacksonville Jaguars fan as of late. articles.title: Raiders Beat Saints, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Cousins, Shough, Bowers, Top Players
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-0 for the first time since the 2021 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-0 for the first time since the 2021 NFL season.

Kirk Cousins led the Las Vegas Raiders to a perfect start with a 35-27 victory over Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints, throwing three touchdown passes in the win.

Despite entering 1-1 against the 2-0 Raiders, the Saints were 3.5-point favorites at home Sunday, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The Raiders silenced the doubters with a fourth-quarter comeback, delivering a dominant 13-0 shutout, delivering on both sides of the ball.

Shough found Juwan Johnson for a short touchdown pass, the lone end zone score of the first quarter, giving New Orleans a 6-3 lead after a blocked extra point.

Las Vegas' offense was rolling in the second, scoring 13 points on two field goals and a Michael Mayer reception while scoring on all three possessions. New Orleans' Shough found Noah Fant for a touchdown to cut the deficit to 16-13 at halftime.

New Orleans responded out of the break with a big third quarter, with Johnson scoring his second touchdown while the defense came up with a big fumble recovery to set up a 47-second drive that ended with Fant finding the end zone for his second score.

Raiders' Mike Washington Jr. stopped the bleeding with a monster 36-yard rushing touchdown to keep the Raiders within five points heading into the final quarter.

The fourth quarter was disastrous for the Saints, who committed four turnovers. The Raiders capitalized with two touchdowns, as Cody White hauled in a pass from Cousins to give Las Vegas the lead before tight end Brock Bowers found the end zone.

Sealing the win, the Raiders came up with a clutch fourth-down sack and forced fumble on Shough, followed by another fumble recovery, to maintain their perfect record.

Las Vegas will host the Kansas City Chiefs next Sunday, while New Orleans will host the Atlanta Falcons the following day for a Monday night matchup.

articles.title: Week 4 Waiver Wire Breakout Fantasy Football Pickups from Sunday's Box Scores
articles.summary: This NFL season has been a difficult one to pin down. The Las Vegas Raiders are 3–0, the winless Atlanta Falcons beat the Green Bay Packers and New England Patriots quarterback and Super Bowl runner-up Drake Maye looks like he forgot how to throw a football.
articles.body:
This NFL season has been a difficult one to pin down. The Las Vegas Raiders are 3–0, the winless Atlanta Falcons beat the Green Bay Packers and New England Patriots quarterback and Super Bowl runner-up Drake Maye looks like he forgot how to throw a football.

The uncertainty has extended to fantasy, as well. So far, preseason expectations for players like Broncos wideout Courtland Sutton, Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts and and Seahawks wideout DK Metcalf haven't come to fruition. Then, as they always do, injuries have complicated the picture further.

Unfortunately, that was the case on Sunday, when star running backs Breece Hall and De'Von Achane of the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins, respectively, left their games due to injuries with their status for Week 4 and beyond.

The players who stepped up in Hall's and Achane's absences are obvious waiver adds, but so too is a rookie tight end who made the most of the opportunities he was given and is confirmed by his coach to be in line for more targets moving forward.

Let's break down which of these breakout players should be on your waiver list for Week 4. To be considered a "breakout" performance, a player must have been rostered in 50% of leagues or fewer coming into Week 3.

Scoring and rostered percentages via FantasyPros .

Week 3 stats: 4 att, 14 rush yds, 3 rec, 3 rec yds, 4.7 pts

One week after posting his first touchdown of the season in the Jets' loss to the Packers, running back Braelon Allen didn't factor much into his team's loss to the Lions, totaling 14 yards on four rushing attempts and bringing in three receptions.

But it's not because of a standout performance this week that managers are going to be submitting waiver claims for Allen ahead of Week 4. The injury-addled New York Jets suffered another wave of losses on Sunday, as lead running back Breece Hall, star wideout Garrett Wilson and guard Dylan Parham all suffered injuries.

While the Jets got good news that Wilson was evaluated and cleared for a concussion, no such update has come for Hall, who was ruled out with a thigh injury .

The Jets are in the top third of the league in terms of rushing yards so far this season, and Hall has had 13 or more attempts in all three games this season. There's plenty of opportunity in the New York backfield; Allen just wasn't seeing much of it before. That could change if Hall is out for the Week 4 matchup against the Bears.

Week 3 stats: 17 att, 41 rush yds, 1 rush TD, 3 rec, 3 rec yds, 14.5 pts

The Dolphins found themselves in a bad spot on Sunday when, at one point, their only two active tailbacks both left the game with injuries.

De'Von Achane appeared to injure his knee early in the game, and while he was initially listed as questionable, he was later downgraded to out. The entire backfield then hinged on backup Ollie Gordon, as Jaylen Wright was inactive with a foot injury.

Gordon shouldered the load beautifully…until he headed to the medical tent, then the locker room, and was deemed questionable to return with cramps. The Dolphins' rushing situation was then truly dire, but thankfully, Gordon was able to return to the game in the fourth quarter.

Unfortunately, the Dolphins may be without Achane for quite some time. Head coach Jeff Hafley said after the game that the knee injury news "does not sound very optimistic."

If Achane has to miss significant time, Gordon has demonstrated that he's capable of producing in his absence…as long as he too can remain healthy.

Week 3 stats: 7 rec, 105 yds, 1 rec TD, 23.5 pts

Not every waiver target this week makes the cut simply because a starter suffered an injury. Some, like Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq, proved that they deserve a spot on your roster by seizing the opportunities they were given and making the most of them.

The Jets rookie had a quiet first two weeks of the season, seeing three targets in each game, though he did log a rushing touchdown in Week 1. However, in the Week 3 loss to the Lions, head coach Aaron Glenn unleashed Saqid and was rewarded for it.

Sadiq saw eight targets, hauling in seven of them for more than 100 yards and a receiving touchdown for 23.5 points.

"Now is the time to throw a lot at him," Glenn said, music to fantasy managers' ears. "He is getting every rep possible to be able to do that." Praising Sadiq's ability to play multiple positions, Glenn added, "We want him to continue to grow in that aspect and try to get him the ball because we saw what he could do."

You heard the man. Submit your claim for Sadiq and hope your rivals weren't paying attention.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley invests up to $500,000 per startup to build wealth beyond the NFL through AI and Bitcoin
articles.summary: Last year, Saquon Barkley offered a glimpse into a financial strategy that looks very different from the usual athlete spending story.
articles.body: Last year, Saquon Barkley offered a glimpse into a financial strategy that looks very different from the usual athlete spending story. The Philadelphia Eagles running back has put a large share of his football earnings into investments, from index funds and real estate to startups linked to artificial intelligence, fintech and emerging technology. His approach comes from a simple concern: an NFL career can end quickly, so he wants his money working long after his playing days are over.Saquon Barkley’s investment strategy began with his NFL earningsBarkley entered the NFL as the No. 2 overall pick in 2018 and signed a $31.2 million rookie contract. Rather than treating that first major payday as spending money, he chose to invest it and rely on endorsement income for his lifestyle.“When I declared for the NFL draft and kind of realized where I was going to be drafted, that was something I was like, ‘You know what? Kind of want to follow the Marshawn Lynch method. I don’t want to touch that. I want to invest it, put it in the right peoples’ hands and learn as I continue to make investments. And just live off the endorsement deals,’” Barkley told ESPN in 2018.That mindset later expanded into private companies. According to The Profile, Barkley has invested in more than 10 startups, with individual investments typically ranging from $250,000 to $500,000. His reported portfolio has included Anthropic, Anduril, Ramp, Cognition, Neuralink, Strike and Polymarket. He has also invested through funds including Founders Fund.Saquon Barkley looks beyond football to build long-term wealthThe motivation behind Barkley’s strategy is closely tied to the short shelf life of an NFL career. A serious knee injury in 2020 forced him to miss most of that season and made the risks of professional football impossible to ignore.“When you sit out of football for a whole year, you realize that this game could be taken away from you,” said Barkley.That experience helped push him towards a wider financial plan. He has invested in traditional assets such as S&P 500 index funds and property, while also taking larger risks in startups and cryptocurrency. In 2021, Barkley announced that he planned to put his endorsement income into bitcoin through Strike.His interest in venture investing grew after reading Peter Thiel’s Zero to One. Barkley has said he studies founders and asks direct questions about their businesses before deciding whether to invest.His approach is not without risk. Startup investments can lose value, and private-company valuations can change sharply. The Profile notes that Barkley understands that trade-off, but he sees ownership as a way to create financial security beyond his time on the field.For Barkley, the bigger picture is clear. Football provides the income, but investing gives him another path to preserve and potentially grow that wealth. articles.body: Richard Sherman has questioned a controversial roughing-the-passer call that helped the Kansas City Chiefs extend their lead over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. With Miami still within striking distance, Chop Robinson was flagged after hitting Patrick Mahomes late in the third quarter. The decision quickly drew attention because Robinson appeared to make an effort to avoid putting his full weight on the quarterback.Richard Sherman questions Chop Robinson’s penalty on Patrick MahomesThe incident happened with Kansas City leading 14-10 and facing third-and-9 near its own goal line. Mahomes released a pass towards Rashee Rice before Robinson broke through the offensive line and made contact with the quarterback.Robinson struck Mahomes around the chest and then fell over him as the play ended. The officials ruled that the defender landed on Mahomes with his body weight and called roughing the passer, giving Kansas City 15 yards and a fresh set of downs.The decision became controversial because Robinson did not appear to target Mahomes’ head or neck. He also extended his arms towards the ground as he fell, seemingly trying to reduce the impact.Sherman, the former NFL cornerback and current analyst, questioned what more the defender could have done in that situation.“Not sure what else the defender can do to avoid the Roughing call other than not trying to make the play,” Sherman wrote on X, sharing a clip of the hit.The NFL has strict protections for quarterbacks, including rules concerning defenders landing with their full body weight. The league says pass rushers must also make an effort to avoid unnecessary contact after the quarterback releases the ball.Patrick Mahomes and Chiefs benefit from controversial callThe penalty proved important because Kansas City turned the extended drive into points. articles.title: Buccaneers fall to 0-3 with loss to Vikings, as Baker Mayfield injures thumb and Todd Bowles' seat gets hotter
articles.summary: The Vikings didn't have a great offensive game but improved to 3-0.
articles.body:
A few coaches were on early hot-seat watch after just a couple games.

Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen helped himself with a win over the Houston Texans . As did Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn with an upset victory over the Seattle Seahawks .

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 0-3 after a home loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and it might have cost them more than just another lost game. On Baker Mayfield 's final pass — an interception after he scrambled on fourth down in the final two minutes — he stayed down on the field injured.

Mayfield was holding his right hand in obvious pain after it was hit on the follow through of his pass. When he walked off the field, he held his hand until he got to the sideline. Mayfield went straight back to the locker room even though there was a chance for Tampa Bay to get the ball back. Bowles said Mayfield had a dislocated thumb and will get an MRI on Monday, via Jenna Laine of ESPN .

And the Buccaneers did get it back after a field goal. Undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels replaced Mayfield for the final 28 seconds. Daniels threw an interception on a Hail Mary and the Vikings held on for a 23-16 win.

If Mayfield misses time, it makes it even harder for Bowles and the Bucs to dig out of their hole. The Bucs are a highly disappointing 2-10 in their past 12 games going back to last season. And once again, the Bucs had the look of a team that is not playing anywhere near its talent level.

Sunday's loss had more sloppy mistakes that have become the norm for the Bucs under Bowles. They gave up an 86-yard punt return TD to fall behind 10-0. A 41-yard touchdown catch by Jordan Addison gave Minnesota a 17-10 lead. A holding penalty wiped out an amazing 85-yard touchdown by Chris Godwin Jr.

After the Buccaneers got an fortunate unnecessary roughness call on a third down, Mayfield and Bucky Irving ran into each other on a handoff for a 6-yard loss and Tampa Bay had to settle for a field goal on that drive. Their entire offense was unprepared to do anything against the Vikings' constant blitzes, including on the final fourth-and-13 when Mayfield had to retreat under pressure and throw a desperation pass that had no shot.

The Buccaneers had a great shot to win because the Vikings' offense wasn't capable of putting the game away. Kyler Murray , returning to the lineup for the first time since suffering a concussion early in the season opener, was ineffective. He completed just eight of his first 21 passes.

Justin Jefferson left the game early with an ankle injury and that didn't help, but overall the Vikings offense had plenty of issues. Over one 10-possession stretch they punted eight times and threw an interception, a ball that was batted at the line by Vita Vea and ended up being hauled in by A'Shawn Robinson.

But the Vikings got the win. They're 3-0. The Buccaneers are on the opposite end at 0-3. And if it doesn't turn around fast — it's unlikely to if an undrafted free agent quarterback has to start games in place of Mayfield — the Buccaneers could be having to ask some tough questions about their head coach.

articles.title: Ravens pull off miracle to beat Cowboys with 7-second drive, Tyler Loop's 56-yard field goal as time expired
articles.summary: The Ravens pulled off a wild win in Brazil.
articles.body:
A seven-second drive? The Ravens found a way to treat Brazil to something American football fans rarely, if ever, see.

The Ravens found a way to win a topsy-turvy game late against the Cowboys on Tyler Loop 's 56-yard field goal as time expired, giving Baltimore an improbable 34-31 victory at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

According to Stathead, this was the first multiplay, game-winning drive of fewer than eight seconds since at least 2001. According to ESPN, it was the latest a winning drive has started since at least 1978 .

The Cowboys tied the game, 31-all, on Brandon Aubrey 's field goal, with seven seconds remaining — a game that appeared destined for overtime. After Aubrey's touchback on the kickoff, Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers on a 27-yard pass play and Jackson quickly called timeout with :01 showing on the clock.

Loop, whose missed kick in Week 18 cost the Ravens a spot in the playoffs last season, finished this game off with the second-longest field goal of his career.

The Ravens improved to 2-1 while the Cowboys fell to 1-2. There were five lead changes in this wild game, including three scores in the final 90 seconds.

The Ravens staked the Cowboys to a 10-point lead early. After an early three-and-out, followed by a turnover on downs, the Ravens started moving offensively. They scored on three straight drives to close out the first half for a 17-13 lead, with Derrick Henry finding the end zone twice. The Ravens then upped the lead to 24-13 on Chris Moore 's TD.

The Cowboys fought back to take the lead after stopping Henry on fourth-and-goal and then drove 96 yards for the go-ahead score.

The Ravens regained the lead after finishing off a late drive on Matthew Hibner's TD catch — his first in the NFL — with 1:28 remaining in the fourth quarter.

Dallas then drove all the way to the Baltimore 2-yard line, but a false start and an incomplete pass on third down forced Dallas to tie the game with the field goal.

The Ravens struck back once again on Loop's epic game-winner, as Dallas left just too much time on the clock.

Jackson threw for 186 yards and two scores and ran for 50 yards. Dallas' Dak Prescott was terrific, too, throwing for 276 yards on 25-of-40 passing. The Cowboys moved the ball well most of the game, but it wasn't enough.

articles.title: Yes, Dak Prescott and Cowboys deserve heat for not scoring a TD late. But Dallas' defense couldn't hold it down for 7 seconds?
articles.summary: Dallas' season isn't over after falling to Baltimore in Rio. But the Cowboys lost the benefit of the doubt, the faith of any remotely impartial observer and...
articles.body:
You never quite know which play will be the one that ruins your NFL season. Sometimes it's obvious, like a game-ending fumble, or cinematic, like throwing a crucial interception. And sometimes it's as painful as a kick to the gut … like, say, when your defense decides with seven seconds remaining in a tie game to play some pillow-soft coverage, setting up a game-losing 56-yard field goal:

The Dallas Cowboys ' season isn't over, not by a long shot. But the Cowboys didn't just lose a football game to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday in Brazil. They lost the benefit of the doubt, they lost the faith of any remotely impartial observer, and they lost any expectation that this porous, injury-ridden, mistake-prone defense is going to get it together anytime soon.

Under normal circumstances, there'd be no shame in losing to Lamar Jackson and the Ravens. And if you look at the numbers without context — Ravens 34, Cowboys 31 — you could believe that maybe this was just one of those games that just didn't go the Cowboys' way.

Not this Sunday. This time, the Cowboys squandered opportunity after opportunity to put this game away, and allowed Baltimore — you know, the team famous for its litany of fourth-quarter collapses — to repeatedly rise from the dead. It's just one game, and not even a division or conference one, but this one ought to sting.

For the Cowboys, the shame of this is that the 2026 season still stretches before them as wide as a 12-lane highway. Coming into the season, the Cowboys had enough talent to inspire Super Bowl predictions. Through two-plus weeks, injuries have decimated two of their three division rivals. Dak Prescott is playing like a quarterback in his prime.

And yet it's impossible to have any faith in this team, primarily because its defense stands about as stout as a wall of toilet paper. Jackson, Zay Flowers and the rest of the Baltimore offense picked apart the Cowboys 20 yards at a time, offsetting some admittedly spectacular plays by Prescott and the rest of Dallas' offense:

Dallas is now 1-2, and inspiring zero confidence. While we're piling on the defense, it's worth noting that Prescott failed to punch in what would have likely been a game-clinching touchdown when he was set up with first-and-goal from the Baltimore 2-yard line with 23 seconds remaining. Two off-target throws, one desperation scramble, and the Cowboys had to settle for a game-tying field goal — which, as it turned out, wasn't nearly enough.

Schottenheimer said after the game that he told Prescott to play it safe on that drive, even to the extent of throwing it away, to preserve the potential field-goal opportunity. That's a sound, if conservative, strategy … but it works only if your defense can stop giving up 20-plus-yard pass plays.

For his part, Prescott put the burden on the shoulders of himself and his offense, saying he was "embarrassed" that they couldn't punch the ball in that final drive. "This one hurts," he said, adding that even after a 10-hour flight home, "I'm sure when we land I'll be just as pissed."

Prescott joined a select quarterback circle on Sunday. He became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to throw for 250 touchdowns and rush for another 30, joining John Elway, Aaron Rodgers , Fran Tarkenton and Russell Wilson . That's some solid company right there. If his defense can help him out by not forcing him to play hero ball every week, the Cowboys might have something here.

Things change fast in the NFL. In three weeks, this game and this stench around Dallas could all be a bad memory. The Cowboys have a favorable three-game slate ahead — at Houston , Tampa Bay, at Green Bay — that could have them at 4-2 when they face the Eagles. But if they falter during this stretch, if the defense can't figure out how to coalesce and Prescott can't close the deal in those crucial moments, it's going to be yet another in a long line of frustrating seasons for Dallas.

articles.title: Jason Kelce joins AI data center backlash as his $200 million Garage Beer brand drops bizarre ad

articles.body: Jason Kelce has found an unusual way to join the growing debate around AI data centers. The former NFL star appears in a new Garage Beer and Liquid Death campaign that pokes fun at the amount of water some data centers can use. The result is an intentionally outrageous commercial featuring Kelce, a jar of urine and a message aimed at the booming AI industry.Jason Kelce takes aim at AI data centers with bizarre campaignLast month, Kelce appeared alongside a Liquid Death can mascot in the advertisement, where he made a deliberately absurd proposal about cooling data centers."AI data centers waste millions of gallons of water," former NFL player Jason Kelce says in the commercial.He then joked about sending urine to data centers for cooling before breaking into a song built around the same gag. The campaign even showed someone taking a jar of urine to a post office.The joke came with a clear disclaimer. The advertisement tells viewers to enjoy a Garage Beer or Liquid Death Sparkling Energy drink before suggesting they send their pee to an AI data center. The small print then makes it clear that viewers should not actually do it.The campaign is tied to a serious issue. Instead, the campaign uses comedy to turn a complicated technology debate into something instantly recognisable.Andy Pearson, Liquid Death's vice president of creative, said the issue has become unusually broad in its appeal."There are many things that Americans can't agree on, but opposition to AI data centers is the one thing almost everyone can agree upon across the political and cultural spectrum," Pearson said.Garage Beer CEO and co-owner Andy Sauer also framed the campaign as a mix of humour and awareness."Water is the world's most valuable resource, and data centers are a hot topic, so we got together to have some fun, while raising a little awareness," he said.The campaign also reflects a wider trend in advertising. articles.title: Dak Prescott Addresses Throwing Ball Away Near George Pickens Late in Cowboys' Loss to Ravens
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys star quarterback Dak Prescott raised some eyebrows with a throwaway in crunch time during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL Rio Game.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys star quarterback Dak Prescott raised some eyebrows with a throwaway in crunch time during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL Rio Game.

With the Cowboys facing third-and-goal with 10 seconds left in the fourth quarter while trailing 31-28, star receiver George Pickens appeared to get open near the pylon, but Prescott already fired the ball past him before he got his head around. After the loss, Prescott admitted to reporters that he was throwing the ball away but should have been more patient to get the ball to Pickens.

Despite Prescott's disappointment in himself, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters that he taught the signal-caller to throw the ball away in that situation.

Prescott was asked about Schottenheimer's direction on the play, but he chose not to get into those details. He said that Pickens was open, and he should have sat on his throw to go for a touchdown.

"Definitely not right now, maybe in a week," he told reporters . "Still fresh, just upset."

Prescott went 25-of-40 for 276 yards and a touchdown in a solid performance, but the Ravens were able to set up Tyler Loop's game-winning 56-yard field goal with one second left on the clock.

The Cowboys fell to 1-2 with the loss. Prescott and Dallas will try to bounce back when they meet the Houston Texans (0-3) in Week 4.

articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 3: Cowboys' clock failures, critical Carolina penalty, and more
articles.summary: The Cowboys mismanaged the final 20 seconds of the game, and the Panthers let one slip away against the Browns.
articles.body:
The momentous plays from Week 2 centered around a few major quarterback injuries. In Week 3, the theme was poor game management and missed opportunities.

There were several wild games on Sunday, and plenty of momentum changes in each of the close contests. A few stood out above the rest.

Here are the most quietly momentous plays from Sunday's afternoon games:

1. The Cowboys blew the final 20 seconds … in multiple ways

Brazil was treated to a wild one, as the Ravens and Cowboys scored three times in the final 90 seconds – with Tyler Loop's 56-yard field goal the game winner .

But the Cowboys badly mishandled the end of the game, with a chance to win. At worst, overtime felt assured. Alas, it was not.

After Nate Wiggins ' pass interference call, the Cowboys were in business at the Baltimore 2-yard line with 23 seconds left, trailing 31-28. Dak Prescott 's first-down pass was incomplete. Then came the first big mistake.

Cowboys tight end Luke Schoonmaker was flagged for a false start, and it completely changed the options Dallas had. It not only moved them back five yards, but it also slimmed down the playbook. With a timeout in their pocket, they could have tried to run the ball on second (or third) down if they wanted to.

But moving it back to the 7-yard line took away the handoff threat. Prescott scrambled on third down — out of necessity — which set up the next mistake. Dallas called a timeout with 14 seconds left, probably leaving too much clock left. They probably could have run it down under 10 seconds, as there is no threat of a 10-second runoff with the clock stopped. Brandon Aubrey 's game-tying field goal could have left the clock far closer to zero.

That led to the third mistake: on the ensuing kickoff Aubrey kicked the ball into the end zone. If the ball is kicked inbounds, the clock runs immediately; those can't be fair caught any longer under the revamped kickoff rules.

It ended with Lamar Jackson hitting Zay Flowers on a 27-yard catch that took only six seconds off the clock, followed by Loop's boomer.

Hard not to think that Brian Schottenheimer could have helped his team's chances with better game-management execution. Twenty seconds doesn't seem like a lot, and we're talking about Dallas arguably leaving a handful of additional ticks on the clock here, but it was just enough for Jackson and the Ravens to pull off a miracle win.

That's the lesson here, one that Michigan fans can affirm quite well: Every second matters.

2. Panthers missing chances in shocking Browns loss

The Panthers outgained the Browns, 391 yards to 276, but they kept kicking field goals and leaving points on the field. They also were on the wrong end of too many big plays in the game.

Midway through the second quarter, Bryce Young was sacked on 4th and 3 in Cleveland territory — the first of three turnovers on downs — which led to a Browns field goal for the first points of the game.

But the real killer came with less than three minutes remaining, with Carolina protecting an 18-13 lead late. The Panthers' Akayleb Evans appeared to intercept Deshaun Watson in the end zone, but Bobby Okereke was flagged for a killer roughing-the-passer penalty.

You decide if this was worth a flag or not:

Watson was hurt on the play and left the game for one snap, but he returned to thread a TD pass to Harold Fannin Jr. for the game winner.

The successful two-point try made it a 21-18 game, and the Panthers couldn't cross midfield as Young was intercepted in the waning seconds. The Browns made more big plays, but the Panthers coughed up a game they could have won.

3. Lions use well-timed blitz to beat Jets

The Lions were perilously close to losing a game they led by 14 points with just over 12 minutes remaining.

The Jets faced a key 3rd-and-17 play in the fourth quarter, and Geno Smith 's pass was incomplete, but D.J. Reed 's defensive pass interference led to a Jets TD, making it a one-score game. After the Lions were stopped on 4th and 1 on the next series, trying to put the game away, the Jets miraculously tied the game on Garrett Wilson 's TD (which was reviewed) and the subsequent two-point play — with Breece Hall knocked out of the game.

Everything was tilting the Jets' way, but the Lions took back the lead, 31-24, on a four-play, quick-strike TD drive.

The Jets were in business to score themselves, using their final timeout with 51 seconds left when Wilson was injured. On second-and-10 at the Detroit 28-yard line, Lions safety Chuck Clark perfectly timed up his blitz and sacked Smith, forcing a fumble recovered by Detroit's Jack Campbell and effectively ending the game.

Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was a few plays away from beating Dan Campbell and the Lions, his former boss and former team, but the Jets couldn't convert when they needed it most late.

4. Darnold 's late pick 6 collapses Seahawks

The Seahawks overcame a 14-point, second-half deficit to tie the game early in the fourth quarter. Even with the Commanders retaking the lead on a field goal, the Seahawks had the ball in Sam Darnold's hands and had driven into Washington territory when disaster struck.

Darnold faced some pressure, never saw Washington's Kain Medrano lurking underneath and threw it right to him. Medrano, who'd never played a defensive snap in the NFL prior to Sunday, undercut the pass, picked it and ran it back 50 yards for a stunning touchdown. That gave Washington a 33-24 lead after the missed extra-point try.

Prior to the pick, it was 2nd-and-15 at the Washington 49-yard line with four minutes left. The Seahawks had all their timeouts, plus the two-minute warning, and trailed only 27-24. There were ample chances remaining for them. Instead, they trailed by two scores late.

The Seahawks actually had a chance to win — and the missed XP loomed large. They drove five plays and 68 yards for a touchdown on a drive that only took 66 seconds. That made it a 33-31 game.

Washington faced a third-and-7 play at the Seattle 44-yard line, and stopping the Commanders there would have given the Seahawks the ball back with a little less than a minute remaining. Seattle was out of timeouts, but a field goal would have won it. Instead, Marcus Mariota kept the ball on a read-option play and gained enough for the first down, giving the Commanders a shocking victory.

Darnold threw for 379 yards and four TDs in his first game back since suffering an oblique injury Week 1, but he was forced into a heavy-pass game when the Seahawks' run game was held to 44 yards. Jadarian Price's lost fumble at his own 20 basically handed the Commanders a free TD early on.

5. Koonce's strip started the Raiders' stirring comeback

In the span of less than a minute, the Raiders turned a three-point edge into an 11-point deficit. New Orleans took a 27-16 lead in a 54-second span of the third quarter with a TD drive, a fumble recovery on the ensuing kickoff, then another TD two plays later.

The Raiders scored to cut the Saints' lead to 27-22, but New Orleans looked poised to make it a two-score game again. At worst, a field goal would have put them up eight points early in the fourth quarter.

The Saints drove to the Las Vegas 29-yard line when Tyler Shough was strip-sacked by Malcolm Koonce , recovered by Maxx Crosby for the Raiders.

Six plays later, Kirk Cousins hit Cody White for a TD that made it a 28-27 Raiders lead. That was the start of the avalanche.

The wheels completely fell off for the Saints, who had been terrific in their first two fourth quarters of the season. That was not the case Sunday. Their four possessions in the fourth: fumble, interception, fumble, fumble.

Shough was guilty of the first three turnovers. Amazingly, even after the Raiders stretched it to a 35-27 lead, the Saints still had a chance to win in the final minutes. They were approaching midfield with just over a minute left when Nakobe Dean stripped Juwan Johnson and Eric Stokes recovered.

The Johnson fumble was big, and we can't overlook Shough's second and third turnovers, but the Koonce strip was the hinge for the Raiders' stirring comeback. What followed were 19 unanswered points. That rally might have come either way, but it shouldn't have started with the Saints only up five points.
