articles.title: “I’m not the same person without both of them”: How Donna Kelce shaped Travis Kelce’s view of women through her work and family life as both a provider and parent
articles.summary: Travis Kelce grew up watching both of his parents contribute to the family. Donna Kelce built a decades-long banking career while raising Travis and Jason.
articles.body: Travis Kelce grew up watching both of his parents contribute to the family. Donna Kelce built a decades-long banking career while raising Travis and Jason. In 2024 Travis explained how that upbringing shaped his view of family and the role women can play within it.His comments came on May 24, 2024 during an episode of “New Heights” while he and Jason Kelce discussed Harrison Butker’s controversial commencement speech.Donna Kelce built a career while raising two future NFL starsDonna Kelce spent decades working in banking before retiring in 2021. Her career included roles at Bank One and KeyBank before she joined Truist. She also worked in affordable housing finance and held senior positions in the banking industry.At the same time she was raising Travis and Jason with Ed Kelce. Ed worked in the steel industry and also remained involved in raising their sons.Donna later spoke about the challenge of balancing work with motherhood. During Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year coverage she said she had worked in banking for nearly 30 years while raising her sons. She also credited her friends and Ed for helping make that balance possible.That experience became relevant when Travis discussed Butker’s comments about women and homemaking.On the May 24 episode of “New Heights” Travis said both of his parents contributed to the family financially and at home.“So they were homemakers and they were providers and they were unbelievable at being present every single day of my life,” Travis said during the podcast.He then connected that family setup directly to his childhood.“That was a beautiful upbringing for me,” Travis said on the same episode.Travis Kelce did not expect every family to follow the Kelces’ exampleTravis also made an important distinction. He did not argue that every household should operate like his own.“I don’t think everyone should do it the way that my parents did,” Travis said during the May 24 episode of “New Heights”.His comments came after Butker’s May 11 commencement speech at Benedictine College. Butker spoke about traditional gender roles and encouraged female graduates to embrace marriage and motherhood.Travis said he disagreed with most of Butker’s remarks. He also said he did not believe he should judge his teammate based on his personal or religious views.His own family offered a different reference point. Donna worked outside the home while raising two sons. Ed also provided for the family. Travis remembered both parents as people who contributed to the household and remained present throughout his childhood.He later explained just how much that upbringing shaped him. “I sure as hell thank my parents and love my parents for being able to provide and making sure that home was what it was,” Travis said during the podcast.He finished with an even more personal reflection. “I’m not the same person without both of them being who they were in my life,” Travis said during the same episode.That gives Donna’s career a deeper place in Travis’ comments. He also saw his father contribute to the family.Travis Kelce’s mom could work and provide while still being a parent. His father could do the same. articles.summary: Sunday nights never seem to disappoint.
articles.body:
It came down to the wire in Denver as the Broncos and Bo Nix pulled off a 30-26 comeback win over Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, fueled by an explosive 30-point second half.

Los Angeles marched into Empower Field at Mile High as a slim 2.5-point favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook but sombered out to cheers of the opposing fans who never gave up after a scoreless first half from Denver.

In the process, Stafford had an up-and-down night, breaking some major NFL records in the loss.

The 38-year-old became the first player to throw for 20,000 yards with two different teams: the Rams and Detroit Lions. He finished his 12 seasons with the Lions with 45,109 passing yards.

On the flip side, Stafford also made history by throwing the most pick-sixes in NFL history, with 33 in total.

The first half was all Los Angeles in the Mile High City.

The Rams led 16-0 at the break behind a touchdown pass to tight end Tyler Higbee and three second-quarter field goals.

L.A.'s defense came up big on the other end, forcing three first-half punts and benefiting from a missed Broncos field goal.

Just when it looked like things were going to go south for Denver, the Broncos came out of halftime looking like a different team, finding the end zone twice in the third quarter, converting both two-point attempts to catch up and knot the game at 16 heading into the final quarter.

Despite an early fourth-quarter interception by Nix, Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga picked off Stafford and returned it 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver its first lead of the game with 4:49 left to play.

Stafford immediately made up for his blunder with a 1:11 drive back down the field, throwing a 48-yard touchdown to Konata Mumpfield to quickly regain a three-point lead.

With one drive left for the Broncos, Nix and his offense stormed down the field, topping off an exciting comeback with Nix diving over the top for a touchdown to take a four point lead with 47 seconds left.

The Rams pushed their way down the field to Denver's 14-yard line with enough time to spike the ball and draw up one more play. Their near-miraculous game-winning touchdown attempt came up short, thanks to Hufanga, who came up with his second interception of the game.

Los Angeles will hit the road to face the Philadelphia Eagles next Sunday, while the Broncos will head to San Francisco to face the 49ers that same day.

articles.title: Rams seemingly on wrong end of questionable pass interference call in loss to Broncos
articles.summary: The Broncos caught a break on a questionable penalty during their final drive.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams probably should have had a key interception in the final two minutes against the Denver Broncos . But Broncos receiver Pat Bryant pulled off a pretty good acting job.

With the Broncos at the Rams ' 11-yard line, trailing 26-23, Bo Nix threw to Bryant. Rams cornerback Josh Wallace made a great interception on the play, getting a knee in bounds, but a penalty flag came out. And in real time it looked like there was contact because Bryant threw up his left and fell to the ground.

A closer look showed that Bryant was embellishing.

Bryant actually pulled Wallace into him, then threw up his hand and flopped down as Wallace made what would have been a game-changing interception. NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay said on the broadcast that he saw no penalty on Wallace.

"We actually see the receiver grab the defender and pull him into him," McAulay said. "I don't see the defender do anything that significantly hinders the receiver on this play."

McAulay clarified that the initial contact early in the play didn't deserve a flag on Wallace either.

"Just hands on him," McAulay said. "He doesn't do anything with it."

The Rams would have had the ball at their own 8-yard line with 1:09 to go. The Broncos had three timeouts left and could have gotten the ball back, but their odds of winning would have dropped dramatically. Instead, the Broncos got a first down and a few plays later Nix scored on a 1-yard touchdown run to give Denver the lead. The Rams had a quick drive to the red zone in the final seconds, but Matthew Stafford was picked off on the final play of the game and the Broncos won 30-26 .

After a report said that Rams head coach Sean McVay ducked out of his postgame news conference, he actually did speak briefly to the media about the loss.

The Rams are off to a 1-2 start . Losing after a penalty that was questionable at best went against them won't help their mood.

articles.title: Cardinals’ 49ers Loss Extends Alarming NFC West Streak
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals‘ performance against the NFC West has gotten historically bad following their most recent loss.Sunday’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers...
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals ' performance against the NFC West has gotten historically bad following their most recent loss.

Sunday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers gives the Cardinals eight straight losses against their NFC West rivals going back to the beginning of the 2025 season. Their record against the NFC West since the start of the 2022 season is a paltry 4-22.

Throughout most of the 2020s, the Cardinals have been the only weak link in the division. Arizona last made the playoffs in 2021, but lost spectacularly to the Los Angeles Rams . They have zero NFC West titles in that timeframe, with their last one coming in 2015.

The Rams and Seattle Seahawks have each won Super Bowls this decade. The 49ers earned a trip to the big game in 2023.

Cardinals Are In Danger Of Embracing The Same Old Script In 2026

Both of Arizona's losses in 2026 have come against divisional opponents, and they offered little resistance. It started with a blowout loss to the Seahawks in Week 2 following an unexpected 1-0 start to the season.

On Sunday, the Cardinals found themselves down 23-6 at one point. While quarterback Jacoby Brissett and Co. got back into the game, the Cardinals never managed to tie or take the lead.

With the Rams appearing to be back on form following a blowout loss in Week 1 to San Francisco , things could get uglier for the Cardinals. What's worse is that the Cardinals seem to have no real identity following the first three weeks of 2026.

Arizona's passing game is inconsistent despite talent in its pass-catching unit. The running game has also struggled through the first three weeks, with first-round pick Jeremiyah Love finally injecting some life into the unit in Sunday's loss when he rushed for 90 yards on 21 carries. Even so, there are still more questions than answers in the Cardinals' backfield.

The Cardinals have also allowed 67 points over their past two contests. Following a game in which 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy threw for 297 yards on just 15 completions , the defense is also showing that it's struggling to stop opponents through the air.

Cardinals Have Enough Talent To Flip The Script

While the Cardinals don't look like playoff contenders at this point, it's not like they're devoid of talent. If Love can enjoy repeat performances, opponents will need to start keying on him. That could open up more opportunities for pass catchers beyond Michael Wilson and Trey McBride .

Marvin Harrison Jr. finally showed flashes in Sunday's loss, notching three catches on five targets for 40 yards. Harrison also hauled in Brissett's longest completion of the day, for 19 yards. Should Harrison build on his improved Sunday performance, he could finally turn into another viable target for Brissett.

But questions remain all over the place on the defensive side of the ball. Through three games, the Cardinals have notched just four sacks. They have also progressively allowed more total yards by the week, bottoming out at 437 against the 49ers. If the Cardinals want to stop this historically bad skid against the NFC West, they must dramatically improve on both sides of the ball.

articles.title: After Kyle Shanahan directs 49ers offense like maestro, players sing his praises
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan has a reputation as a clever play-caller. After the banged-up team beat the Cardinals on Sunday, his players sai...
articles.body:
The good news for the already comically depleted San Francisco 49ers : Even if this attrition never ends, they still might have a chance if Kyle Shanahan remains available for the final 14 regular-season games.

The black-and-blue 49ers played most of the second half Sunday without two future Hall of Fame offensive players - wide receiver Mike Evans and left tackle Trent Williams - and no one noticed because the head coach is a Canton-level play caller.

The 49ers' first-half numbers in their 36-30 win over the Cardinals at Levi's Stadium: 17 points, nine first downs, 227 yards. Their second-half stats: 19 points, 14 first downs, 210 yards.

How does that happen when the after-halftime wide receiver corps consisted of past-his-prime Deebo Samuel and Three Guys, and quarterback Brock Purdy 's blindside was protected for the final four drives by - let's check the roster here - Vederian Lowe ?

Right guard Dominick Puni had a ready explanation. Shanahan could generate offense with the kids at Santa Clara High.

"You talk about injuries, but when you have coach Shanahan out there, it's almost like - I'm not saying it doesn't matter - but he just puts us in such good positions all the time," Puni said. "You can never doubt him. Ever. He's probably the biggest weapon we have on offense."

If Puni was getting carried away, it's hard to blame him after Shanahan played a critical role in Purdy (297 yards, four TDs, 133.8 passer rating) carving up the Cardinals.

Purdy's second pass: He had a 2-yard completion to Evans on 3rd-and-12, Evans pitched to Samuel and Samuel sprinted 80 yards down the left sideline on a hook-and-lateral touchdown.

"Obviously, a great play call in that moment," Purdy said.

Purdy's final pass: With the 49ers leading 29-27 with 1:36 left, the Cardinals out of timeouts and everyone expecting a 2nd-and-10 run, Purdy rolled right on a play-action bootleg and tossed a turn-out-the-lights 20-yard touchdown pass to tight end George Kittle . The nearest Cardinals defender was in Cupertino.

"I thought it was a great play call," Purdy said.

Sensing a theme? It started before Sunday. Shanahan has opened the season on a three-game heater.

In Week 1, Shanahan's game plan called for Purdy to paper cut the Rams to shreds in 27-7 win: 11 of Purdy's 25 completions were thrown behind the line of scrimmage. In Week 2, Shanahan called for a deep-ball deluge in a 35-13 win over the Dolphins: Purdy completed 10 of 10 passes for 211 yards on passes at least 10 yards beyond the line of scrimmage.

The result: After three games, Purdy is completing 72.3% of his passes. That would be a franchise record. He has a 133.1 passer rating. That would be an NFL record.

He's on pace to throw 51 touchdown passes and six interceptions while directing an offense that Sunday became the first since the 2014 Bengals to not allow a sack in the season's first three games, and he'll happily explain that he's not doing it alone.

"I think Kyle's the best in the league at calling plays, his system," Purdy said. "But calling the right plays at the right time. I think that's the difference between a good play caller and a great play caller. You can have all the plays drawn up but to call a play at the that's what it takes to be elite.

"We're all grateful to play for him. We know that anytime a play call comes in, we're confident that we have the best in the league at doing this."

Said Williams: "The best player caller in the NFL. For sure. One-hundred percent."

Given their ongoing attrition, the 49ers will likely need Shanahan to stay in The Zone to remain undefeated after hosting the Broncos next Sunday and visiting the Super Bowl champion Seahawks on Oct. 11.

On offense, Evans (ribs/oblique), who appears likely to miss at least one game, joined sidelined wide receivers De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson , who are on injured reserve with ankle injuries. Meanwhile, the 49ers' defense finished Sunday's game without seven of nine defensive linemen who made their initial 53-man roster. Seriously.

The state of the defense meant it was no surprise Sunday's game was a shootout. And that could be why Shanahan, who generally saves his trick plays for big moments in big games - think "Skyy Bang Reverse Pass" in January - surprised the Cardinals with razzle-dazzle on the 49ers' third offensive snap.

Kittle noted part of the cleverness in the call: The pitchman on the play, Evans, is a regular third-down target.

"Everybody's going to expect us to throw the ball to Mike Evans," Kittle said. "So that was cool."

Said Puni: "That was pretty badass. I mean, who thinks to do that in that situation?"

The same question could be asked of Purdy's final pass. The 49ers figured to try to drain the clock. Instead: A dagger to an all-alone Kittle.

"I was so excited when they called that play," Kittle said. "The way that they'd been running downhill, that whole drive they were doing six (players) on the line, I was, like, 'I'm going to be uncovered here.' And I was uncovered."

Kittle did make a mistake by scoring. If he'd taken a knee before reaching the end zone, the 49ers could have run out the clock in a 29-27 win. Instead, the Cardinals got the ball back, kicked a field goal with 34 seconds left and had a chance to pull off an improbable comeback if their onside kick had been successful.

"That's on me," Shanahan said. "I didn't remind (Kittle) in the huddle. I don't expect him to be paying attention to the clock. But I definitely wish I did (tell him) the play before that."

Yes, the coach is in a zone. Even when he screwed up Sunday, his offense scored six points.

articles.title: NFL Week 3 Sunday takeaways: Patriots have a Maye problem, Chargers hit rock bottom and Cowboys crumble
articles.summary: Biggest Week 3 NFL takeaways incldue Drake Maye struggling with six interceptions, and Brock Bowers returning from knee surgery in stunning fashion.
articles.body: We spend all offseason waiting for football to come back and somehow we're already three weeks into the NFL season. I'd appreciate it if things could slow down a little. Although, if you're a fan of the Dolphins, Titans or Chargers, you probably think the season can't go by fast enough. Week 3 gave us plenty to talk about, and I have some thoughts. Here’s my biggest takeaway from each of Sunday’s games. Bills 24, Chargers 16 Takeaway: It was a good week for Buffalo to come out flat. Buffalo's offense came out of the gate with a 36-point output against a stout Houston defense in Week 1 and then followed it up by dropping 41 on Detroit in Week 2. But the unit struggled mightily on Sunday, turning the ball over three times on its first four possessions. After managing to get the game tied at 10 going into halftime, the Bills turned it over on their first two possessions of the second half. Lucky for them, they were playing the awful winless Chargers, who couldn't even beat a team that turned the ball over five times. Buffalo can't play like that against good teams. Browns 21, Panthers 18 Takeaway: Sorry, Deshaun Watson, I wasn't really familiar with your game. Insert Shaq meme here. Yeah, so, I buried Watson after a horrendous performance in Week 1 (following a terrible preseason). But he played pretty well against the Bucs in a Week 2 win and did enough to lead the Browns to a shocking 2-1 record. Watson's numbers don't look great (16-30, 144 yards, 2 TD), but he kept making big throws when the team needed them and added some important runs to keep the chains moving. Watson isn't great, obviously, but he's at least playing like a serviceable NFL quarterback and that's more than I expected from him after Week 1. DESHAUN WATSON GOES FROM CLEVELAND VILLAIN TO HERO IN BROWNS UPSET WIN, AS HOME CROWD TURNS JEERS TO CHEERS Lions 31, Jets 24 Takeaway: The Jets really aren't that bad. Speaking of teams for which I didn't have high expectations, the Jets have been much better than I expected. Yes, they're 1-2. But they should have beaten the Packers in Week 2 and they were tied with the Lions with under three minutes left. Now, great teams win those games. The Jets aren't great. But given that the bar was set at, like, below average, Jets fans have a reason to at least have some hope for the first time in years. Colts 19, Texans 17 Takeaway: The AFC South is bad again. You know, for a minute it looked like the AFC South might be good again instead of being relegated to that Saturday afternoon Wild Card slot (the one that goes to the least interesting first-round playoff matchup). But here we are with the Colts and Texans both not looking particularly good. C.J. Stroud has never regained his rookie season form and Daniel Jones turned the ball over three times. Plus, these teams just aren't even fun to watch (the Jaguars really aren't, either, and don't get me started on the Titans). Just put the winner of this division at 4:30 on Wild Card Saturday now and be done with it. Jaguars 35, Patriots 6 Takeaway: Drake Maye looks like a one-hit wonder. I'm trying not to overreact but Maye keeps making it harder and harder. He's made some of the worst throws of any quarterback so far this season, and that's saying something. The Patriots offense has generated just two touchdowns in three games and Maye has thrown six interceptions and has lost a fumble. With a game in Buffalo next week, it could start getting late early for the reigning AFC champions. TREVOR LAWRENCE FANTASY OWNERS ARE BESIDE THEMSELVES AFTER INEXPLICABLE DECISION IN FOURTH QUARTER BLOWOUT Chiefs 24, Dolphins 10 Takeaway: The Dolphins showed some fight? I don't know, what do you want me to say? The Chiefs beat the Dolphins, as literally everyone expected. Miami hung around for a while and was only down four heading to the fourth quarter. But Kansas City still won by two touchdowns. Dolphins fans have only one date on their minds: April 29, 2027 (the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft). Giants 12, Titans 7 Takeaway: Two bad offenses playing in bad weather is a recipe for a bad game. I have four TVs in my living room and thanks to multiview, I can essentially watch every NFL game simultaneously. I do my best to keep my eyes moving so I can watch as much of each one as possible. But I'm not going to pretend I spent much time watching Jameis Winston and Cam Ward battle on a wet field to see who could get to double-digit points first. It was the Giants, by the way, and they won. Woo-hoo. Steelers 30, Bengals 27 Takeaway: I tried to warn you. I wrote in my NFL picks column this week that the Bengals were due for a letdown and the Steelers were likely to show up at home and finally play a solid offensive game. There was no chance I was going to let this perfect "I told you so" moment pass. That being said, this doesn't change my opinion: The Bengals are still good, the Steelers still aren't very good. It was one game and I'm not reading too much into it. Commanders 33, Seahawks 31 Takeaway: Turnovers matter a lot, folks. No, I don't think the Commanders are better than the Seahawks. No, I don't think the Commanders are better with Marcus Mariota at quarterback instead of Jayden Daniels. But I do think that winning the turnover battle is massively important (unless you're the Chargers) and Washington had 3 takeaways to Seattle's 0. That's why the Seahawks lost despite outgaining the Commanders 437 to 258. 49ers 36, Cardinals 30 Takeaway: What a weird game this was. The 49ers appeared to be on their way to an easy victory after taking a 23-6 lead four minutes into the second half. But give credit to the Cardinals, who just never quit. At the same time, San Francisco never trailed and every time Arizona got within one score, the 49ers would score a touchdown (except the final time, but the game was over at that point). The bigger concern is that San Francisco saw three key players leave the game with injuries: Mike Evans, Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw. Vikings 23, Buccaneers 16 Takeaway: Kevin O'Connell is a magician. The Vikings are 3-0 because O'Connell is legitimately a top-five coach in the NFL (maybe top three). It almost doesn't even matter who the quarterback is because KOC will scheme his way into victories. More importantly, though, the Bucs screwed me over this week and I'm not going to miss an opportunity to whine about that. I'm officially over Tampa Bay. BAKER MAYFIELD LEAVES GAME AFTER WRITHING IN PAIN ON TURF IN TAMPA BAY WHEN THUMB ON THROWING HAND INJURED Raiders 35, Saints 27 Takeaway: Welcome back, Brock Bowers. Bowers angered fantasy football managers (including myself) by undergoing knee surgery just before the start of the season (without any major indication there was a problem prior to most fantasy drafts), but he reminded everyone that he's not really human. Not only did he return from meniscus surgery in less than 20 days, but he immediately went out and caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. Don't look now, but the Raiders are 3-0 with a showdown against the Chiefs coming in Week 4. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Ravens 34, Cowboys 31 Takeaway: Ball don't lie. The referees nearly gifted the Dallas Cowboys a win with an awful pass interference call that set the Cowboys up on the Ravens 2-yard line trailing by 3 points with 23 seconds left in the game. Dallas ultimately didn't score a touchdown, kicked a field goal to tie, then inexplicably allowed the Ravens to easily pick up 27 yards in 6 seconds to give Tyler Loop the opportunity to boot a game-winning 56-yard field goal, which he did. The team that should have won did win, and that doesn't always happen in the NFL so we should be grateful for that. Broncos 30, Rams 26 Takeaway: Sean Payton remains the most overrated and luckiest coach in the NFL. If you've read my NFL columns before, you probably saw this one coming. If you're new, welcome! I'm Dan and I think Sean Payton is the NFL's most overrated head coach. Once again, Payton benefited from something outside his control, this time a terrible pass interference call on what should have been a game-winning interception by the Rams. Instead, Denver kept the ball and scored a game-winning touchdown a few plays later. Payton is a good coach that the media treats like an elite coach because he's nice to them. But that reputation glosses over his up-and-down record, the Bountygate scandal that no one seems to talk about anymore and just how much he benefited from landing Drew Brees (only because the Dolphins medical staff screwed up royally). Denver won despite Nix completing just 50% of his passes for under 200 yards with an interception.

articles.title: NFL's most debated Week 3 call has people wondering how to defy gravity when hitting Patrick Mahomes
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins edge rusher Chop Robinson's hit on Patrick Mahomes drew a roughing the passer flag that reignited debate over NFL quarterback rules.
articles.body: The Miami Dolphins are winless, which isn't good, but it gets worse because they also don't have a sack this season, making them the NFL's only team bearing that stigma. And all that made Sunday's controversial call sting all the more. The Dolphins today are going to dissect the fact they thought edge rusher Chop Robinson hurried Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes to throw the football out of the end zone for a big fourth-quarter stop. The ball fell harmlessly incomplete. PATRICK MAHOMES ANSWERS TROUBLING QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS SERIOUS KNEE INJURY ON FIRST DRIVE OF THE CHIEFS SEASON The way Mahomes fell was much more harmful in the view of the officials, who promptly called Robinson for roughing the passer. And why did Robinson get called for the controversial penalty? Because he landed on Mahomes without somehow sufficiently showing that he was trying to avoid stuffing the great quarterback into the Hard Rock Stadium grass. Remember that word – stuffing – because, believe it or not, it's an actual NFL rulebook standard for calling roughing the passer. (But first, full transparency: This penalty didn't change the outcome of the game. It didn't really affect the Chiefs at all because there was another Dolphins penalty on the play that would have extended the possession anyway.) But this penalty speaks to what lengths the NFL is going to protect its quarterbacks., how much latitude flawed officials get in making a call, and to what degree defenders are supposed go to avoid hurting QBs. That degree perhaps includes floating in air. Maybe levitating for a beat or two. Or simply defying gravity. Robinson didn't do any of those. He hit Mahomes and the quarterback went down. "No, he got me," Mahomes said afterward. "He got me for sure pretty good. But that’s part of playing football." Part of playing football is requiring pass rushers to somehow tackle the quarterback but "not unnecessarily or violently throw him down or land on top of him with all or most of the [defender's] weight," per the NFL rules book. And here's the problem 1: It's in the official's sole judgment if the defensive player did his best to not land with full weight on the quarterback. Problem 2: Defenders cannot typically hit the quarterback square and then stop their progress while in mid air. "Those are tough, man. Those are tough," Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks said. "... I personally don't think that Chop was wrong in anything he did, and so that's something that we can't control." It's understandable the Dolphins cannot control this because neither can anyone else. It's physically impossible for a 280-pound dude to stop falling once he's in the air. He also cannot change the trajectory of his fall so as to avoid the guy he just hit. NEW NFL FINE SCHEDULE IS GOING TO A POINT SYSTEM THAT COULD LEAD TO SUSPENSIONS BUT ALSO REFUNDS The only way coaches have figured out to coach this is for rushers to try to cushion their fall with their arms and hands. You know, act like they didn't fall as hard as gravity demanded. That's what this call left Robinson thinking about – how to put his hands out with such drama as to allay the referee's fear that the face of the NFL was on the ground. "Put my hands out earlier," Robinson told reporters at his locker stall after the game. "I did what I was taught to do..." What makes this so difficult is the rule itself. NFL Rule 12, Section 2, Article 11 defines roughing the passer, and protecting any player in a passing posture from unnecessary, late, or violent contact. It states: "The Referee has principal responsibility for enforcing these rules. Any physical acts against a player who is in a passing posture (i.e. before, during, or after a pass) which, in the Referee’s judgment, are unwarranted by the circumstances of the play will be called as fouls." So, yes, this is all "the referee's judgment." And then the weight-bearing problem that brings the stuffing action into play... "A rushing defender is prohibited from committing such intimidating and punishing acts as 'stuffing' a passer into the ground or unnecessarily wrestling or driving him down after the passer has thrown the ball," the rule reads. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "When tackling a passer who is in a defenseless posture (e.g., during or just after throwing a pass), a defensive player must not unnecessarily or violently throw him down or land on top of him with all or most of the defender’s weight. "Instead, the defensive player must strive to fall to the side of the quarterback’s body, or to brace his fall with his arms to avoid landing on the quarterback with all or most of his body weight." Robinson braced his fall with his arm. But apparently the referee weighed the defender's fall and decided he followed through with all or most of his body weight. Or maybe it's just an faulty rule that needs more work. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Austin Ekeler Reportedly to Sign Commanders Contract, Latest Fantasy Advice for Waiver-Wire Decision
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders are planning to sign veteran running back Austin Ekeler, according to Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders are planning to sign veteran running back Austin Ekeler, according to Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.

Ekeler spent the previous two seasons in Washington. He logged just two appearances in 2025 after suffering a torn Achilles.

The 31-year-old joins a backfield that includes Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White, so he's likely to provide depth more than anything else. From a fantasy football perspective, his return to the nation's capital shouldn't have fantasy managers rushing to the waiver wire.

Ekeler had a stretch where he was one of the more dynamic running backs in the league. He led the NFL in touchdowns scored in 2021 and 2022 and finished with at least 1,500 yards from scrimmage three times between 2019-22.

A high-ankle sprain caused Ekeler to miss three games in 2023. He was diagnosed with two concussions in 2024, costing him a total of five games. Then came the Achilles tear, which could have big implications on his performance moving forward.

The Commanders are looking for something to spark their running game. Croskey-Merritt went for just 36 yards on 19 carries in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks.

White has been more effective as the backup but picked up a shoulder injury Sunday. Prior to signing with the Commanders, his four-year spell with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers wasn't all that impressive.

And quarterback Jayden Daniels is recovering from a dislocated elbow. Whenever he does return, the team won't want him scrambling out of the pocket much, thus taking another dimension away from the ground game.

Maybe Ekeler makes an impact as a situational ball-carrier and pass-catcher out of the backfield. It's tough to envision him getting enough touches to merit any serious fantasy consideration.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 3 Game vs. Panthers
articles.summary: An absolutely dominant performance from the defensive front and timely playmaking on offense led the Browns to a 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 3.
articles.body:
An absolutely dominant performance from the defensive front and timely playmaking on offense led the Browns to a 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 3.

The Browns are now 2-1, tying them with the rest of the AFC North through three weeks of the season.

It's not a position many expected the Browns to be in, but they've gotten a lot of key contributions from their young core. Throw in just enough improvement from Deshaun Watson and Cleveland played winning football in their home opener.

Let's break it down by doling out grades for the key players on Sunday.

For three quarters, Deshaun Watson could best be described as "meh". Going into the fourth quarter, he was 10-of-21 passing the ball for just 67 yards.

But he kept the ball out of harm's way and extended some drives with his scrambling.

The most important positive was that he was able to turn things around in the fourth quarter and come through in the clutch. His touchdown pass to Harold Fannin to retake the lead looked like vintage Watson. He scrambled to his left, extended the play against pressure and threw a dart to Harold Fannin.

It's hard to say he won the game for the team. The defense kept them in the ballgame for three quarters, but he didn't lose it.

The running back remains the hardest player to grade on the Browns offense right now. The run game was better. How much of that was the Panthers defense being notoriously bad at stopping the run is hard to suss out.

Judkins had 70 yards, but he still didn't crack 4 yards per carry and his longest of the day was 11.

It doesn't help Judkins' case that Sanders lone carry of the day went for 17 yards. He also trucked Jaycee Horn after catching a ball in the flats. Sanders brought real juice to the offense in his role.

The stat line says that KC Concepcion only caught two of his nine targets for 17 yards on the day.

It won't tell you that Watson missed him badly on at least three of those targets. The rookie still needs to do more with the ball after the catch, but the low production wasn't all on him.

Boston probably needs more than four targets a game at this point. He brought down two of them for 41 yards and remains the Browns only consistent threat down the field. He was kept out of the endzone, but still had the longest reception (28) of the day for the Browns.

It continues to be perplexing why the Browns won't give Tylan Wallace and/or Isaiah Bond more run. Jeudy played 36 snaps and didn't see a single target. It's time to play some younger guys with some upside.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode 🗣️

Fannin reminded everyone how good of a weapon he can be for the offense. He caught both of Watson's touchdown passes and picked up some of the chain-moving responsibilities of Concepcion.

Not only did he score twice, but he created three first downs with his seven receptions.

Whiteheart wasn't targeted in the passing game, but some of the Browns best gains on the ground came in two-tight end sets. His blocking helped Cleveland do some good things in the run game.

There were some growing pains for Fano against the Panthers. He was beaten by second-year edge-rusher Princely Umanmielen on an inside move after oversetting for the speed rush.

He also picked up a brutal holding call that set them back to 2nd-and-20.

Johnson easily had his best game as Brown. He wasn't at fault for much of the Panthers success in the pass rush and he was helpful in opening up a few more holes this week.

All three interior blockers' grades should take a hit for getting beat across the board on the fourth-and-short that could have iced the game with a minute left.

Jenkins put together a clean pass protection performance at the pivot. The run game also was the best it has looked in part because of his blocking in the middle.

The rookie guard got a taste of what it's like to block one of the best interior defenders in the league. Derrick Brown is a tough test for anyone in the league. Barber was beaten for a pressure on the first drive and it wasn't the last time.

He'll have to improve his anchor against the better bull rushers in the league to take the next step as a starter.

The case for playing Dawand Jones at right tackle grew stronger on Sunday. Howard was flagged for three more false starts after picking up at least one in each of the first two games.

It's not like the penalties are the only thing hurting Howard. He's looking for a head start because he is not holding up well in pass protection.

The Browns defensive front was the MVP of this game and Jared Verse was a huge reason for it. After a slow start in the first two games, he led the way with a team-high six pressures, per Next Gen Stats .

The first two games he attracted game plan attention to open the way for others. This week, he delivered himself. Still waiting on the first sack, but Verse was altering Young's play in the pocket.

McGuire also showed up in a game where Bryce Young was constantly under duress. He beat rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling multiple times.

The most crucial came on third-and-goal at the end of the first half. He turned the corner on the rookie and forced a field goal with a sack.

Barnett continued to provide meaningful snaps on the defensive line. He joined the pressure party on a few occasions and chipped in a batted pass to the cause.

It's still too early to say that Mason Graham is an All-Pro player, but he certainly looked like one on Sunday. Graham finished the day with seven tackles, two sacks and three tackles for a loss. He was even better than his statline, though.

Huntington was the only defensive lineman who didn't register at least one pressure, per PFF . He didn't have a run stop either. He wasn't an outright liability against the run, though.

Hall got called for a questionable roughing the passer. Not going to ding him too much for it because it isn't a call that would happen every time and it wasn't the only time he put some pressure on the quarterback.

The elder statesman of the interior group was a factor in beating up the Panthers offensive line. He only had three tackles, but he registered two quarterback hits on the day.

Schwesinger had his least productive tackle day. He had just one solo stop with five assists to get to six total. Still, he was strong in coverage and didn't have any major lapses.

The defensive line's dominance made his day easier than usual. He wasn't forced to clean up a lot.

Williams was the downhill thumper against the run that the Browns need. He wasn't stellar in pass protection, but he usually tackled the receiver who caught the ball against him.

A nice hit on Bryce Young as a blitzer boosts the grade a bit as well.

Lockdown. That's a one-word summary, but we'll expand a bit more here. Tet McMillan had two strong performances going into this one. He was held to just two receptions for 17 yards and Ward shadowed him all day.

Blackmon stepped in for Tyson Campbell who was out with hip and ankle injuries. Targeting him was definitely in Carolina's gameplan. He was mostly fine until he gave up a 31-yard bomb to Brycen Tremayne on a 3rd and 4 to end the third quarter.

Harden wasn't an absolute liability on Sunday, but he also wasn't an asset in the way he was last week when he had an interception. The Panthers' tight ends were able to have success going against the linebackers and Harden.

Delpit had a rough day in coverage. According to PFF's tracking , he allowed five catches on six targets and Bryce Young had a passer rating of 105.6 when targeting the safety.

The game-ending interception was nice. However, he was at fault for some of the success the Panthers had in passing to their tight ends. He had a much better day as a run defender.

Szmyt kicked two field goals through the uprights, including a 48-yarder.

Bojorquez was busy on Sunday with five punts. He averaged 48.6 and thre of the five were downed inside the 20. That's nice work.

Corley committed the cardinal sin of failing to secure the football on the opening kickoff of the second half. The rest of his returns were unremarkable.

The 2026 NFL season is readying its approach to the first-quarter mark of the campaign.

How is fantasy football life treating you so far?

Ideally, you're setting sights on an unblemished 4-0 start. But if you're hovering around .500 or even starving for your first victory, fear not—There is time to turn things around.

You just need to flip that switch sooner than later. That requires both deft handling of your current roster and shrewd navigation of the waiver wire, but luckily, we're here to help with both. While laying out our early rankings at the marquee positions for Week 4, we'll also touch on priority targets off the waiver wire for each spot.

Waiver-wire target: Marcus Mariota, WAS (vs. IND)

Mariota's first start in place of a hobbled Jayden Daniels looked similar to Mariota's relief appearance last week: pretty efficient and productive through the air, pretty quiet on the ground. It'd be great if Mariota's rushing impact increased, but he is streamable without it if he keeps throwing like this (30-of-47 for 294 yards and four scores so far).

Projected stats: 20-of-30 for 201 yards, two touchdowns; four rushes for 19 yards

Waiver-wire target: Ollie Gordon II, MIA (at MIN)

De'Von Achane suffered a worrisome injury Sunday, and Gordon immediately got to work on picking up the slack. While Gordon was far from great, his impressive volume perhaps pointed toward some great outings in his near-future: 17 carries, three receptions (on three targets) and Miami's only touchdown. If Achane misses significant time, Gordon has a chance to make significant noise.

Projected stats: 18 carries for 74 yards, one touchdown; three receptions for 29 yards

Waiver-wire target: Keenan Allen, IND (vs. HOU)

Alec Pierce landed on IR on Saturday, and Allen immediately seized his opportunity. Now, this wasn't Allen's first chance to make an impact (he was targeted 11 times over the first two weeks), but he still made these opportunities count (six catches on nine targets for 63 yards and a score). And with Pierce missing a minimum of four games, those opportunities should keep coming Allen's way.

Projected stats: Seven receptions for 72 yards, one touchdown

articles.title: NFL News: Insider Updates Timeline for Josh Jacobs Return to Green Bay Packers
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List as the National Football League attempts to […]
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List as the National Football League attempts to obtain video footage of him allegedly striking his girlfriend this offseason. With that pursuit ongoing, it appears the Pro Bowl running back won't be seen on the field anytime soon.

During an appearance Sunday on NFL Network's NFL GameDay , insider Ian Rapoport said that a return to the team isn't "imminent" for Jacobs and it could be weeks before he even has a chance at being cleared to play.

"If they get to the point where it's five games, six games, maybe eight games, that might be when you're looking at a potential return for Josh Jacobs." Ian Rapoport on when Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs could return

"If they get to the point where it's five games, six games, maybe eight games, that might be when you're looking at a potential return for Josh Jacobs."

Ian Rapoport on when Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs could return

Jacobs was placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List before Week 1 while the league attempted to obtain video of the alleged battery incident. It has since filed a Freedom of Information Act request after the judge ruled against a request from both sides in the case for the video to be sealed.

Under NFL rules, every game Jacobs misses this season while on the exempt list counts toward any future suspension he receives. For example, Jacobs spending the first six weeks of the 2026 NFL season on the exempt list and then receiving an eight-game ban from the league would mean he could return in Week 9 against the New England Patriots .

Examining Green Bay Packers Rushing Stats Without Josh Jacobs

With Jacobs out, the Packers offense has relied on a three-man rotation at running back with MarShawn Lloyd , Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson through three games. It's resulted in the worst rushing offense in the NFL.

Entering Week 4, Green Bay ranked last in rushing yards per game (48.7) with the second-worst rushing offense ( Denver Broncos ) sitting at 81.0 rush ypg . For further comparison, 20 NFL teams are averaging more than twice as many rushing yards per game as the Packers offense averages.

MarShawn Lloyd, who looked promising in training camp, has stayed healthy for the first time in his NFL career but he's averaged just 3.0 yards per carry on 23 attempts with poor vision and a lack of explosion being very apparent.

Kaleb Johnson, the 83rd overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft by the Pittsburgh Steelers , has also struggled. He's second on the team in carries (12) and has begun earning more snaps than Lloyd, but he's also shown no real ability to create yards for himself.

The Packers offensive line is also plenty responsible for the team's inability to run the football, with right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele out for the season, left guard Aaron Banks missing two of three games and guards Jager Burton and Jacob Monk both struggling. So, even if Jacobs returns to the field, it seems unlikely that Green Bay's rushing attack will improve significantly this year.
